Through proactive problem-solving, equipment optimization, and close collaboration with cross-functional teams, you will contribute directly to manufacturing excellence, product quality, and the company's overall competitiveness.You will join a highly skilled and interdisciplinary team of approximately 40 engineers, technicians, and support specialists. Our working environment is built on openness, trust, and collaborative teamwork, providing an atmosphere where technical expertise is valued, innovation is encouraged, and both professional and personal development can thrive.Key ResponsibilitiesEquipment Ownership- Provide technical support, optimization, and further development of production equipment within the EGIO area (Epitaxy, Glass Processes, Implantation, and Furnaces).- Ensure high equipment availability and process stability.- Conduct fault analysis and implement sustainable corrective actions.- Coordinate and oversee preventive maintenance and repair activities.Process and Quality Optimization- Analyze equipment and process data to identify improvement opportunities.- Develop and implement initiatives to improve: - OEE (Overall Equipment Effectiveness)- MTBF (Mean Time Between Failures)- MTTR (Mean Time To Repair)- Process Capability (Cp/Cpk)- Yield and Product Quality- Perform statistical analyses and root-cause investigations.- Support the qualification of new processes, products, and equipment upgrades.Project Management- Lead and participate in cross-functional improvement projects.- Plan and implement equipment upgrades and retrofit programs.- Collaborate with equipment manufacturers, suppliers, and external service providers.- Prepare technical specifications and requirement documents.Production Support- Support escalation management within the manufacturing environment.- Deliver technical training for operators and maintenance technicians.Other Responsibilities- Ensure compliance with safety, environmental, and quality standards.- Maintain equipment performance in line with production targets.- Reduce unplanned equipment downtime.- Document technical modifications and engineering changes.- Support audits and ensure compliance with regulatory and corporate requirements.EducationBachelor’s or Master’s degree in one of the following disciplines:- Electrical/ Mechanical/ Microsystems/Process Engineering- Physics- Materials Science- Or a comparable technical fieldProfessional Experience- Minimum 3 years of experience in the semiconductor industry or a comparable high-tech manufacturing environment.- Practical experience in at least one of the EGIO responsibility areas.Technical Expertise- Strong understanding of semiconductor manufacturing processes.- Knowledge of SPC (Statistical Process Control), FDC (Fault Detection and Classification), APC (Advanced Process Control), and data analytics.- Experience with MES and ERP systems.- Familiarity with vacuum technology, high-temperature processes, gas delivery systems, and cleanroom technologies.- Ability to interpret technical drawings, electrical schematics, and engineering specifications.Personal Competencies- Strong analytical and structured approach to problem-solving.- High level of initiative and ownership.- Ability to work effectively in interdisciplinary teams.- Excellent communication skills across all organizational levels.- Resilience and flexibility in a dynamic manufacturing environment.- Continuous Improvement mindset.Language Skills- Fluent in German and English, both written and spoken.- Ability to communicate effectively with international suppliers and development partners.Reporting Line: Service & Maintenance Managers and the Section About NexperiaAt Nexperia, legal expertise is a key enabler of our global business strategy. As a leading international semiconductor company, we operate in a complex, fast-moving environment where high quality legal advice truly matters. We are looking for an experienced Senior Legal Counsel who combines strong corporate and M&A expertise with business acumen and a collaborative mindset.About the roleIn this senior role you:- Provide corporate legal support and ensure corporate compliance for the global Nexperia group, including Nexperia Germany and the Hamburg site (which includes corporate housekeeping and ESG).- Act as secretary to the Nexperia Germany Board of Directors.- Support the Deputy Chief Legal Officer ("DCLO") on specific matters in strategic corporate projects, such as in the field of Corporate/M&A, Finance, Tax and Treasury (which includes M&A, investments, strategic co-operations (incl R&D), intercompany agreements, treasury and insurance matters).- Deliver commercial legal support to certain key customers under the supervision of the DCLO.- Are managing disputes, litigation and claims (such as distributors, local suppliers etc).- Are managing outside legal counsel and legal spend.- Support the German Corporate Affairs department.The role is based at our office in Hamburg, and you will report directly to the Deputy Chief Legal Officer.What you will needThe ideal candidate has 6-10 years of relevant experience as a corporate lawyer or (in-house) legal counsel and is ready to further apply and deepen their expertise in an international environment.Furthermore, you have:- A completed university degree in law.- A truly international mindset and have excellent communication skills in English (written and verbal).- Strong knowledge of and experience in corporate law and ESG in an international setting.- Relevant experience gained at a leading law firm and/or a multinational company (considered as an advantage).- M&A experience (considered a strong advantage).- Experience working closely with Finance, Treasury and/or Tax departments.- Litigation experience (considered an advantage).- Proven experience working with C‑suite and senior management stakeholders.
